entities.name: Texoma
entities.coverage_notes: Texoma is the primary cross-state coverage region for Texoma Weekend Guide, connecting North Texas, southern Oklahoma, Lake Texoma and nearby destinations represented in the directory.
entities.editorial_boundary_description: TWG uses Texoma as an editorial cross-state region rather than a single political jurisdiction. On the Texas side, routine coverage centers on the Texoma and North Texas communities in the guide, with US-380 used as the normal southern boundary. On the Oklahoma side, coverage focuses on southern Oklahoma communities and destinations represented by TWG, including the Lake Texoma area, Durant, Ardmore, Sulphur, Atoka and nearby communities.
entities.description: Texoma is a cross-state region spanning North Texas and southern Oklahoma, with Lake Texoma and the Red River forming a central geographic and cultural connection between the two states. Texoma Weekend Guide uses the region as its primary editorial coverage area for local events, businesses, venues, restaurants, attractions, parks, lodging, lake recreation and weekend destinations.
entities.short_description: The Texas–Oklahoma region at the heart of Texoma Weekend Guide.
entities.history_summary: Texoma is commonly used for an interstate region divided between Texas and Oklahoma. The name combines Texas and Oklahoma, while Lake Texoma—created by Denison Dam and designated Lake Texoma in 1944—became one of the region’s defining destinations.
entities.visitor_summary: Explore events, businesses, venues, restaurants, attractions, parks, lake recreation and weekend destinations across the Texas and Oklahoma sides of Texoma.

entities.name: Grayson County
entities.coverage_notes: Grayson County is a core Texoma Weekend Guide coverage area. TWG covers events, businesses, venues, attractions, parks, recreation and communities throughout the county, including Sherman, Denison, Pottsboro, Whitesboro, Howe, Van Alstyne, Gunter, Bells, Collinsville, Tioga, Tom Bean, Whitewright and surrounding areas.
entities.short_description: Lake Texoma, historic communities, local events and North Texas destinations at the heart of the Texas side of Texoma.
entities.description: Grayson County sits along the Texas-Oklahoma border in North Texas, with the Red River and Lake Texoma forming much of its northern edge. Sherman serves as the county seat, while Sherman and Denison form the county's principal urban centers. The county combines Lake Texoma recreation, historic downtowns, parks, cultural attractions, restaurants, live entertainment, rural communities and rapidly growing North Texas cities. Texoma Weekend Guide uses this county guide to connect visitors and residents with current events, businesses, venues, attractions and city guides throughout Grayson County.
entities.history_summary: Grayson County was created by the Texas Legislature on March 17, 1846, from territory previously included in Fannin County. It was named for Peter Wagener Grayson, an attorney general of the Republic of Texas and prominent figure in the Texas independence era. The act creating the county also provided for a county seat named Sherman. Agriculture shaped much of the county's early economy before railroad development accelerated growth in the 1870s. The creation of Lake Texoma in the 1940s added a major recreation, tourism and water resource along the county's northern boundary.

entities.name: Sherman
entities.coverage_notes: Sherman is a core Texoma Weekend Guide community and the county seat of Grayson County. TWG coverage includes Sherman events, businesses, venues, restaurants, attractions, parks, arts, entertainment, shopping and other local destinations.
entities.description: Sherman is the county seat of Grayson County and one of the principal communities of North Texas and the Texoma region. The city combines a historic downtown, Austin College, parks, arts and entertainment, restaurants, shopping, community events and growing commercial development. Texoma Weekend Guide connects visitors and residents with current Sherman events, venues, attractions, businesses and places to explore.
entities.short_description: The Grayson County seat and a major North Texas and Texoma center for events, dining, culture, education and local attractions.
entities.history_summary: Sherman was founded in 1846 by the Grayson County commissioners and named for General Sidney Sherman, a hero of the Texas Revolution. The original townsite was approximately four miles west of the present city, but a lack of wood and water led to Sherman's relocation to its present site in 1848. Sherman was incorporated in 1858. The city developed as an important commercial, governmental, educational and transportation center, with Austin College moving to Sherman in 1876 and numerous other educational institutions helping establish the city's historic reputation as an educational center.
entities.visitor_summary: Explore Sherman events, live music, restaurants, historic sites, parks, family activities, arts and entertainment, shopping and other things to do. Sherman also provides convenient access to Denison, Lake Texoma and destinations throughout Grayson County.
